comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the ATG5-retromer interaction claims (C3, C38, C40, C41, C42, C50, C51) well-supported by APEX2 proximity labeling, co-IP, and control experiments. Both rate as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find GLUT1 missorting in ATG5 KO cells (C5, C52-C57) well-supported by HCM quantification, colocalization studies, and biochemical data. Both rate as SUPPORTED and recognize this as a core finding.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations strongly support the distinction between canonical autophagy and atg8ylation (C9, C63-C67). Both recognize the epistasis experiments and genetic dissection as key evidence demonstrating independence from canonical autophagy. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support the Rab7 mislocalization findings (C70-C73) showing atg8ylation-dependent but autophagy-independent effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED without methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support the ATG2A/B and VPS37A knockout data (C82-C84) as evidence for the broader model linking atg8ylation to endolysosomal homeostasis and retromer function. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the systematic knockout analysis of atg8ylation components (C7, C58, C60-C62) showing consistent GLUT1 missorting phenotypes. OpenEval emphasizes unchanged retromer protein levels; peer reviewers focus on the extension to multiple autophagy genes. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the VPS35 KO phenotype and lysosomal damage response (C43, C44, C46-C49). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation; peer reviewers accept findings and note the ALIX recruitment distinction. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Significant disagreement. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, concluding that general atg8ylation (not CASM specifically) is required based on ATG16L1 complementation experiments (C75-C81). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'the direct mechanism by which ATG8ylation regulates the retromer remains unsolved' and noting CASM's role is unclear.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support ATG5's unique dual role (C87-C89, C110-C112) based on differential phenotypes and co-IP data showing reduced retromer complex integrity. Both rate as SUPPORTED and recognize this as explaining ATG5-specific effects.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the overarching conclusions about noncanonical ATG5 and atg8ylation roles in retromer function (C90-C94, C121). OpenEval emphasizes the dual mechanism model; peer reviewers accept the main conclusions as providing novel insights. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap. OpenEval R12 addresses conjugated vs unconjugated ATG5 interaction with retromer (C112). Peer R9 includes C112 among claims supporting ATG5's unique role. Both find this mechanistic detail supported, though peer review integrates it into broader dual mechanism discussion.

OpenEval finds CI-MPR missorting data (C85) SUPPORTED but appropriately notes it as a minor, likely indirect effect. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this would likely be accepted given the cautious interpretation.
